reach an agreement “to not do any horse tripping, cattle prodding, tail pulling” and the like.</p><p>“We believe” steer tailing “is inhumane treatment toward animals, it is horrific, it should be prosecuted, we believe it falls under the Humane Care for Animals Act,” which her boss, Will County State’s Attorney James Glasgow, was involved in creating years ago.</p><p>That said, a new law specifically targeting steer tailing would help “clarify for the judiciary that this is an abuse,” Renken said, noting some in the judicial system have questioned whether it falls under the existing statute. “And it’d also simplify the process for prosecutors.”</p><p>“We are zealous about this and would work with anyone about drafting legislation” that all sides “would be comfortable with,” Renken said.</p><p>Elyssa Ford, an associate professor of history at Washington State University who has studied rodeos, echoed that, saying it's important for any legislative discussion to be "inclusive."</p><p>"There are things that are hundreds of years old that we as a society" now "say is not OK," Ford says. "We’ve seen this with bull fighting."</p><p>If and when steer tailing is further legislated out of practice in the U.S., it should "include various constituent groups and interest groups in those conversations."</p><p>In 2023, Glasgow’s office prosecuted a rodeo rider from Batavia for beating a horse during a Joliet area rodeo in an incident that also was captured on video by a SHARK drone.</p><p>In Ogle County, west of DeKalb County, a permit for a rodeo was recently surrendered following a lawsuit by SHARK and others.</p><p>Wiederkehr got into trouble in Ogle County last year for calling dispatchers to report animal abuse at the venue and, unsatisfied police weren’t going to be sent, said there was a shooting in an apparent attempt to force a response.</p><p>She was convicted last month of false reporting and harassment but hasn’t been sentenced.</p><p>Her attorney is seeking a new trial.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/environment/2026/06/16/smooth-greensnake-prairies-peggy-notebaert-nature-museum-study-forest-preserves" target="_blank" >Tiny snake native to Illinois prairies faces new hurdles in Chicago region and beyond</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/environment/2026/05/22/american-robins-chicago-illinois-midwest-declining-environmental-factors" target="_blank" >American robins’ numbers are on the decline. entries.title: 15 more Chicago campuses join Sustainable Community Schools program
entries.summary: <p><i>This story was </i><a class="Link" href="https://www.chalkbeat.org/chicago/2026/08/03/fifteen-more-schools-join-sustainable-community-schools-program/" target="_blank" ><i>originally published</i></a><i> by Chalkbeat. Sign up for their newsletters at </i><a class="Link" href="https://ckbe.at/newsletters" target="_blank" ><i>ckbe.at/newsletters</i></a><i>.</i></p><p>Chicago Public Schools will open 15 more Sustainable Community Schools this upcoming school year, meaning roughly 10% of district schools will receive extra funding to partner with nonprofit organizations and provide wraparound support for students and families.</p><p>Mayor Brandon Johnson announced the expansion Monday morning at Malcolm X College, where he was joined by allied Chicago Board of Education members, Chicago Teachers Union President Stacy Davis Gates, and several educators whose schools are part of the program or are joining this year.</p><p>There are now 51 schools in the program, which CPS launched in 2018 with the CTU. A <a class="Link" href="https://www.chalkbeat.org/chicago/2025/12/19/chicago-public-schools-sustainable-community-schools-initiative-problems/" target="_blank" >Chalkbeat</a> <a class="Link" href="https://www.chalkbeat.org/chicago/2025/12/19/chicago-public-schools-sustainable-community-schools-program-cost-outcomes/" target="_blank" >analysis</a> last year found the schools have mixed outcomes and have left millions of dollars unspent. The district’s contract with the union requires 70 schools to join the initiative by the end of <a class="Link" href="https://contract.ctulocal1.org/12-2.html" target="_blank" >its contract in 2028.</a> Of the city’s roughly 630 public schools, which includes charters and others run by independent operators, 520 are run by the district.</p><p>Schools in the program receive $500,000 annually to work with a community-based organization and provide extra programming and support for students and parents, such as hiring more mental health professionals. Schools must apply to join.</p><p>Johnson said the expansion connects to his vision of creating more resources for communities, such as more affordable housing and "holistic solutions" to violence.</p><p>"This model provides more than an education," he said. "It is the hub of wraparound, academic, and social support that’s extended to the entire community."</p><p>The expansion is a sign that the "days of school closures, consolidation, and privatization has ended officially," Johnson added — a potential nod to <a class="Link" href="https://www.chalkbeat.org/chicago/2026/05/27/51-candidates-running-for-the-2026-chicago-school-board-election/" target="_blank" >candidates for school board</a> he doesn’t align with, who may be interested in closing schools in response to CPS's dipping enrollment.</p><p>District officials, the union, and school leaders have described the program as a godsend for schools with lots of students from low-income families. The office that oversees the Sustainable Community Schools program is slated to spend about 57% more than it budgeted last year, from about $24.6 million to $38.6 million, according to the district’s <a class="Link" href="https://www.cps.edu/globalassets/cps-pages/about-cps/finance/budget/budget-2027/docs/fy27-revised-budget-book--2.1.pdf" target="_blank" >latest budget book.</a></p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-080000" name="module-080000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><b><u>New Sustainable Community Schools</u></b><br><ul id="rte-287ff122-90e5-11f1-8cdc-3f783ddaa671"><li>Chicago High School for the Arts</li><li>Chicago Vocational High School</li><li>Roberto Clemente Community Academy</li><li>DeWitt Clinton Elementary School</li><li>Mary E. Courtenay Elementary Language Arts Center</li><li>Marie Sklodowska Curie Metropolitan High School</li><li>James Farmer, Jr. Elementary School</li><li>Foster Park Elementary School</li><li>Gage Park High School</li><li>Mildred I. Lavizzo Elementary School</li><li>Little Village Elementary School</li><li>Roswell B. Mason Elementary School</li><li>Benjamin E. Mays Elementary Academy</li><li>Parkside Elementary Community Academy</li><li>Theodore Roosevelt High School</li></ul></div> </div><p>But since the program’s launch, schools and their partner organizations have <a class="Link" href="https://www.chalkbeat.org/chicago/2025/12/19/chicago-public-schools-sustainable-community-schools-initiative-problems/" target="_blank" >left more than $6.6 million unspent</a>, according to a Chalkbeat analysis last December. Chalkbeat also found that internal tensions and staff turnover sometimes strained partnerships between schools and nonprofit organizations.</p><p>Student outcomes are <a class="Link" href="https://www.chalkbeat.org/chicago/2025/12/19/chicago-public-schools-sustainable-community-schools-program-cost-outcomes/" target="_blank" >mixed.</a> Schools that originally joined the program now have higher graduation rates than schools that didn’t get into the program. Suspensions dropped among all schools in the program, as they did at similar schools outside the program. But chronic absenteeism is higher, and enrollment is lower, at participating schools.</p><p>To combat some of these challenges, CPS changed how schools join the program, said Megan Hougard, chief of college and career success at CPS.</p><p>Previously, schools and organizations did not meet before schools applied, she said.</p><p>This year, CPS expanded the list of nonprofits that schools can partner with. Interested schools then met with the organizations, picked which one to work with, and applied together, Hougard said.</p><p>Now, she said, "there’s shared expectations, and then there’s just a checkpoint of, 'Is this the right match?'"</p><p>One of the new schools in the program is Gage Park High School on the Southwest Side. Mike Norwood, a physical education teacher at Gage Park told the crowd at Malcolm X that he "almost started crying" when his principal told him the 300-student school had been selected. He said the school has a strong environment but “needed a miracle” to help boost resources for its neediest students.</p><p>The opportunity will allow the school, which is partnering with the Southwest Organizing Project, to create more clubs and activities for kids, such as job training, he said.</p><p>"It takes a village to raise a child," he said. "Now, it takes a school to raise a community."</p><p><i>Chalkbeat Chicago bureau chief Becky Vevea contributed.</i></p><p><i>Reema Amin is a reporter covering Chicago Public Schools. Contact Reema at </i><a class="Link" href="mailto:ramin@chalkbeat.org" target="_blank" ><i>ramin@chalkbeat.org.</i></a><i> </i></p><p><i>Chalkbeat is a nonprofit news organization </i><a class="Link" href="https://www.chalkbeat.org/chicago/2026/08/03/fifteen-more-schools-join-sustainable-community-schools-program/" target="_blank" ><i>covering public education</i></a><i>.</i></p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/education/2025/08/04/cps-designates-16-new-sustainable-community-schools" >CPS designates 16 new ‘sustainable community schools’</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/education/2024/02/09/mayor-brandon-johnsons-sprint-to-remake-chicagos-public-schools" >Mayor Brandon Johnson’s sprint to remake Chicago’s public schools</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/education/2018/08/08/cps-and-ctu-to-turn-20-schools-into-community-hubs" >CPS and CTU to turn 20 schools into community hubs</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Lab owner pleads guilty in $300 million coronavirus testing scheme tied to ex-Loretto Hospital executive
entries.summary: <p>A lab owner pleaded guilty Wednesday to bilking the federal government out of hundreds of millions of dollars as part of a coronavirus testing scheme tied to former Loretto Hospital Chief Financial Officer Anosh Ahmed.</p><p>Mohamed Sirajudeen, 53, from Chicago, is the first person convicted in the two pending criminal cases involving Ahmed. Charges were previously dropped against two of their co-defendants in the testing scheme amid allegations of prosecutorial misconduct that surfaced when the "Broadview Six" case collapsed.</p><p>Sirajudeen and the other defendants in that case were <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2025/06/17/former-loretto-hospital-executive-charged-fake-covid-testing-scheme" target="_blank" >accused of attempting to defraud the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services</a> out of nearly $900 million through fraudulent COVID-19 testing claims. Prosecutors said roughly $300 million was paid out, and more than $200 million went to Sirajudeen's business, O'Hare Clinical Lab Services.</p><p>The feds’ probe of Ahmed and Loretto Hospital dates back to 2021, when Block Club Chicago reported the hospital had shared COVID-19 vaccines with employees at Trump Tower, where Ahmed had a condo. The vaccines were just becoming available and were still rare.</p><p>Ahmed lawyer Matthew<b> </b>Carter<b> </b>revealed in court last week<b> </b>that Ahmed<b> </b>would <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/07/29/loretto-hospital-fraud-anosh-ahmed-broadview-six" target="_blank" >no longer fight<b> </b>extradition<b> </b>from<b> </b>Serbia</a>, where he’s been held in custody since November. The announcement came after U.S. District Judge Sharon Johnson Coleman shot down<b> </b>a request to toss his charges in the testing scheme over claims of prosecutorial misconduct.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/23/broadview-six-boutros-mecklenburg-loretto-hospital" target="_blank" >Sheri<b> </b>Mecklenburg</a>, the prosecutor accused of mishandling the “Broadview Six” grand jury, has faced similar misconduct allegations in Ahmed’s case.<b> </b>The<b> </b>feds<b> </b>already<b> </b>avoided<b> </b>a hearing<b> </b>about the allegations<b> </b>in June by <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/11/broadview-six-grand-jury-misconduct-federal-prosecutors-drop-charges-loretto-hospital-covid-fraud" target="_blank" >permanently dropping charges</a><b> </b>against Ahmed's two co-defendants. </p><p>But Ahmed will likely seek similar treatment once he's arraigned by U.S. District Judge Sharon Johnson Coleman. And she's <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/10/hearing-in-loretto-hospital-case-could-address-claims-of-prosecutors-misconduct-if-feds-dont-drop-it" target="_blank" >clearly interested</a> in holding an evidentiary hearing<b> </b>about the allegations that have rocked the Dirksen Federal Courthouse this summer.</p><p>Late Tuesday, Chicago U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros sought to get a handle on the Broadview case, which has been engulfed his office in a credibility crisis unlike any faced by his recent predecessors.</p><div class="Enhancement" Vazquez/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>In a court filing, Boutros argued that there's <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/05/boutros-broadview-six-perry" target="_blank" >no need for sanctions or a special counsel</a> in the case, which targeted a group of Operation Midway Blitz protesters who are mostly involved in local Democratic politics. The case fell apart in May after U.S. District Judge April Perry became aware of Mecklenburg's apparent misconduct before the grand jury that heard both the Broadview and Loretto testing cases.</p><p>U.S. District Judge Robert Gettleman<b> </b>handles Ahmed’s other criminal case, involving <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2024/07/12/loretto-hospital-cfo-15-million-embezzlement" target="_blank" >a $15 million embezzlement scheme</a> at Loretto. Gettleman hasn't been asked to settle questions tied to Mecklenburg’s alleged misconduct.</p><p>Sirajudeen pleaded guilty to money laundering during Wednesday's hearing in Johnson Coleman's courtroom. His sentencing has been delayed because he's cooperating with prosecutors. </p><p>Ahmed hired Sirajudeen in June 2022 to submit bogus biological samples for COVID-19 testing and perform tests on Loretto's behalf, even though Ahmed was no longer affiliated with the hospital, prosecutors said. The arrangement was intended to make the samples appear legitimate so Sirajudeen’s lab could submit reimbursement claims to the government.</p><p>Prosecutors said Ahmed used the identities of about a million purported patients for testing at Sirajudeen’s lab, falsely claiming they were uninsured and had submitted biological samples for coronavirus testing, even though they hadn't.</p><p>Under the agreement, Sirajudeen paid Ahmed a fee for each specimen sent to his lab for processing, prosecutors said. Sirajudeen submitted $642.1 million in claims to the government and received about $201.7 million in reimbursements. Sirajudeen then paid Ahmed more than $147 million.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2025/06/17/former-loretto-hospital-executive-charged-fake-covid-testing-scheme" target="_blank" >Former Loretto Hospital executive accused in $293 million fake COVID-testing scheme</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/05/boutros-broadview-six-perry" target="_blank" >Boutros acknowledges ‘mistakes’ in ‘Broadview 6' case but says sanctions, special counsel aren’t needed</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/07/29/loretto-hospital-fraud-anosh-ahmed-broadview-six" target="_blank" >Indicted ex-Loretto exec’s return to U.S. could add to feds’ ‘Broadview 6' headaches</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>
